config.prompt: Piaget's engine — pair each concept with what it does:

pairs.right: new experience fits the old schema — a toddler who has 'dog' extends it to a cat
the schema changes — dog gets split from cat
the grasp that things persist when hidden — emerging around 8 months
the three-mountains failure: the child cannot describe a scene from another's vantage

config.why: When predictions keep failing, the system seeks equilibration — a better theory. Children are active theory-builders, not sponges.

activities.anchor: The stage theory has aged badly in its details
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a Piaget briefing
activities.name: devStageSpot

config.prompt: One line of this Piaget briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Children fail Piaget's tasks for mixed reasons — language load, memory demands, the oddness of repeated questioning.
Small redesigns let younger children pass: hide a smaller policeman's office and 3-4-year-olds stop searching where the doll can see them.
Children's thinking differs qualitatively from adults', not just in amount.
The stage ages are a timetable children must meet on schedule.
config.correction: The ages were lower bounds from small samples and demanding tasks — modern methods put most competencies years earlier, and stage boundaries blur into continuous, uneven growth.
config.why: A child can be a formal thinker about football and a concrete thinker about chemistry — the method (watch children fail systematically) is what changed the field.

activities.anchor: The overturn came from a method trick
activities.caption: scrub the dated studies of the lesson
activities.name: devStudiesTimeline

events.title: Harlow's monkeys
events.text: Infants raised with wire mothers that fed them and cloth ones that did not spent their time on the cloth — contact comfort attaches.

events.title: Ainsworth's Strange Situation
events.text: Mother, stranger and two separations, coded on reunion behaviour: secure, insecure-avoidant, insecure-resistant.

events.title: The Sally-Anne task
events.text: Baron-Cohen, Leslie and Frith: most 4-year-olds say Sally will look where she left the marble — the false-belief leap around age four.

events.title: Baillargeon's drawbridge
events.text: At 4-5 months, infants look reliably longer at the impossible event — they expected the box to still exist.

events.title: Wynn's arithmetic
events.text: A 5-month-old watches 1 + 1 dolls go behind a screen; when one is revealed, looking time spikes.

events.title: Hamlin, Wynn and Bloom
events.text: 6- and 10-month-olds reach for a puppet that helped a climber over one that hindered it — a preference for helpers.

events.title: The marshmallow reanalysis
events.text: Watts, Duncan and Quan, with a larger, more diverse sample, cut the delay-of-gratification effect roughly in half.

activities.anchor: Hold the enthusiasm at the right voltage
activities.caption: bet on the safest summary
activities.name: devReplicationPredict

config.q: Several infant-cognition findings have weakened in large-scale replications, and ManyBabies exists to audit the field. What is the safest summary?
choices: The looking-time method is worthless and should be abandoned
Piaget's search tasks were right all along
Infants are far more competent than Piaget's search tasks implied, but 'moral baby' claims run ahead of the evidence
Every infant-cognition finding has replicated perfectly
config.why: Looking-time effects are inferences from differential looking, they require careful controls, and the field now demands pre-registered, multi-lab designs — competence yes, headline morality not yet.

config.prompt: From ZPD to internalised thought — order the arc:
items: Assistance is pitched just beyond independent reach — the zone of proximal development
Support is gradually withdrawn as competence grows
Private speech — narrating one's own actions — goes underground and becomes planning
config.why: Testing with assistance is more predictive than testing alone, because it measures the growing edge rather than the frozen past — and private speech increases on hard tasks, the opposite of what a pure-maturation view expects.

activities.anchor: Harlow's monkeys (1958) supplied the mechanism's edge
activities.caption: drag the divider — wire versus cloth
activities.name: devHarlowCompare

before.label: the wire mother — provided food
before.text: Fed the infants, yet received almost none of their time.

after.label: the cloth mother — provided comfort
after.text: Fed nothing, yet the infants spent their time on the cloth — contact comfort, not food, attaches.

config.why: Bowlby's synthesis behind it: infants are born to seek proximity to a protective adult because, across evolution, that behaviour kept them alive — building an internal working model of self-worth and other-reliability.

activities.anchor: awareness of how language itself works
activities.caption: true or false — the bilingual myth
activities.name: devBilingualJudge

statements.s: The milestone clock runs the same for bilingual children as for monolingual ones.
statements.why: Growing up with two languages neither delays nor confuses development.

statements.s: Growing up with two languages delays or confuses language development.
statements.why: The misconception — early exposure is what matters, and more of it harms nothing.
Awareness of how language itself works is one of the dividends.

statements.s: Deaf babies exposed to sign babble manually — the syllable engine is modality-general.
statements.why: Babbling around six months in the hands as in the voice: the clock runs on nearly any modality.

activities.anchor: That asymmetry is the modern reading of teenage risk-taking
activities.caption: call the remodelling horizon
activities.name: devPfcEstimate

config.prompt: Into about what age does the prefrontal cortex — planning, impulse control, weighing consequences — keep remodelling?
config.why: The mid-20s, while reward circuitry matures earlier — a strong accelerator with brakes still being installed, especially when peers are watching: adolescents take far more risks in company than alone in driving-simulator studies.
config.context: Executive function — working memory, inhibition, flexibility — predicts school outcomes broadly.
